reference.title: Headings
reference.becomes: A heading. `#` to `######` give the six levels, and a line of `=` or `-` under the text gives the first two.

cases.name: links inline, by reference, in angle brackets, to a file and to a heading
cases.example:
An [inline link](https://example.com "Title"), a [reference link][ref], <https://example.com>, [a file](Other%20note.md) and [a heading](#a-heading).

[ref]: https://example.com
cases.view: An inline link, a reference link, https://example.com, a file and a heading.

reference.title: Links
reference.becomes: A link showing its text. A click opens it in Rich view, and Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on a Mac) in Rich editor. A reference link's definition is left out of Rich view.

reference.title: Pictures
reference.becomes: The picture, from the workspace, or from an https address while `tandemMarkdown.images.allowRemote` is on. A picture that cannot be shown says why in its place.

cases.name: a table cell draws what a line draws
cases.example:
| What | Example |
|---|---|
| Formatting | **bold**, `code` and ==marked== |
| Links | [[Other note]] and #active |
| Math | $E = mc^2$ |
| Emoji | :tada: |
cases.view: WhatExampleFormattingbold, code and markedLinksOther note and #activeMathE=mc2Emoji🎉

reference.title: Table cells
reference.becomes: A cell draws what a line draws: formatting, links and wikilinks, tags, emoji, math, footnotes, pictures and HTML, each under its own setting. What is a block by nature, such as a contents list or a block id, shows as typed in a cell, and an embedded note shows as a link to it. A `|` in a cell is written `\|`, in a link's shown text and a picture's size too.
